description: A writer that dies while holding <id>.run-state.lock (after lock create, before unlink) leaves the lock forever; every later save of that run returns code `locked` until a human deletes the file. The lock file is created empty (no pid, host or time), so neither the store nor an operator can tell a dead holder from a live one. Stray <id>.run-state.json.<uuid>.tmp files from the same crash are never reaped. Also: the lock is removed in a finally whose unlink error is swallowed, so a failed unlink (antivirus EPERM) after a SUCCESSFUL save leaves a permanent lock while the save reported ok. A store whose purpose is resuming after a crash blocks resume after a crash. Not merge-blocking (unwired; limit stated in the manifest NOT-covered section); BEFORE-WIRING condition.
repro: child process: createRunStateStore(root, {...realRunStateFs, rename: () => process.exit(9)}).save('r1', null, state); then a fresh createRunStateStore(root).save('r1', null, state) -> {ok:false, code:'locked'}; directory holds r1.run-state.lock and r1.run-state.json.<uuid>.tmp (real NTFS, Windows Server 2025, node 24.19)
fix_direction: write owner {token,pid,host,at} into the lock; takeover only by the claim-then-rename protocol and rules of qa/contracts/t037-join-rules-store-lock.md (G1, age > staleMs AND pid ESRCH, no moving of a possibly-live lock), with an interleaving test; reap tmp files older than the lease; or alert on `locked` with a runbook. Surface a failed lock unlink.

description: Under real cross-process contention on Windows, opening the lock with flag wx fails with EPERM (file just unlinked by another process, delete pending) in addition to EEXIST. takeLock only maps EEXIST to `locked`, so the caller gets `io-error` for what is plain retryable contention. No state was lost (3 processes x 60 CAS increments finished with counter 180 = 180, no lost update), but a wired caller that treats io-error as fatal would abort a run that should have retried.
repro: 3 node processes, each looping {load; save(expected=loaded, next=counter+1)} until 60 successes against one root on NTFS: per process io-error 6, 3, 4 (EPERM, open <id>.run-state.lock) beside locked 924/977/1070 and conflict 4/7/8; final counter 180
fix_direction: map EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY on the lock create to `locked` (or bounded retry like the rename), and test with real processes (the existing lock tests use only the in-memory fake).

description: Two mutants survive all 18 tests: (a) temp file created in a different directory than the target (path.join(path.dirname(root), ...) instead of `${file}.${uuid}.tmp`), which on a real volume boundary turns the atomic rename into EXDEV or a copy; the fake fs accepts a cross-directory rename; (b) canonical() replaced by JSON.stringify, so an `expected` with keys in a different order than the stored state would spuriously conflict (the real code accepts it: verified). A third survivor is near-equivalent: lstat -> stat differs only for a file symlink, which this machine cannot create without privilege.
repro: mutate run-state-store.ts: const tmp = path.join(path.dirname(root), `${runId}.${fs.uuid()}.tmp`) -> 4 test files pass; mutate runStateRevision to JSON.stringify -> 4 test files pass
fix_direction: assert in the fake that rename source and target share dirname; add a CAS test with a key-reordered expected; add one real-fs test that a temp file is created beside the target.
